\section{Notations}\label{appendix:notations}
We detail below useful notations and basic properties used throughout the appendix.
\begin{itemize}
    \setlength\itemsep{0.3cm}
    \item[-] \(\llbracket T \rrbracket := \{1, 2, \dots, T \} \quad, \forall T \in \N^* \)
    \item[-] \(\cste : \text{Universal constant, i.e. independent of \(S,d,K, T, \kappa, \kappa_*\)} \)
    \item[-] \( \lambda := (S+1) Kd \log(T/\delta) \qquad \text{(regularisation parameter)} \)
    \item[-] \(\kappa_*^{-1} = \rho^\top \nabla \mu(\theta_* x_*) \rho \)
    \item[-] \(\kappa := \max_{\lVert\theta\rVert\le S} \max_{x\in\X}  \tfrac{1}{\lambda_{K-1}(\nabla\mu(\theta x))} \)
    \item[-] \(\ell_{t+1}(\theta) := \sum_{k=1}^K - \mathbbm{1}[k=y_t] \log(\mu(\theta x_t)_k) \)
    \item[-] \(\diam(\Theta) = \max_{x\in\X}\max_{\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta} \lVert (\theta_1 - \theta_2) x \rVert_2 \)
    \item[-] \(H_t(\theta) := \sum_{s=1}^t \nabla\mu(\theta x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \)
    \item[-] \(\bar H_t(\theta) := \sum_{s=1}^t \nabla\mu(\theta x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \sum_{s=\tau+1}^{t-1} \tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K} \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \)
    \item[-] \(W_t := \sum_{s=\tau+1}^{t-1} \nabla \mu(\theta_{s+1}' x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \)
    \item[-] \(\bar W_t := \sum_{s=\tau+1}^{t-1} \nabla \mu(\theta_{s+1}' x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \sum_{s=\tau+1}^{t-1} \tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K} \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \)
    \item[-] \(g_t(\theta) := \sum_{s=1}^t \mu(\theta x_s) \otimes x_s + \lambda \theta \)
    \item[-] \(G_t(\theta_1, \theta_2) := \sum_{s=1}^t \int_0^1 \nabla \mu((v \theta_1 + (1-v)\theta_2)x_s)dv \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \)
    \item[-] \(g_t(\theta_1) - g_t(\theta_2) = G_t(\theta_1, \theta_2) (\theta_1 - \theta_2) \qquad\text{(Mean-value Theorem)} \)
    \item[-] \(\alpha_s(\theta_1, \theta_2) := \int_0^1 \nabla \mu(((1-v) \theta_1 + v\theta_2)x_s)dv \otimes x_s x_s^\top \)
    \item[-] \(\alpha_s(\theta_1, \theta_2) = \alpha_s(\theta_2, \theta_1) \qquad\text{(change of variable)} \)
    \item[-] \(\tilde \alpha_s(\theta_1, \theta_2) := \int_0^1 (1-v) \nabla \mu(((1-v) \theta_1 + v\theta_2)x_s)dv \otimes x_s x_s^\top \)
    \item[-] \(\alpha(\theta_1 x_1, \theta_2 x_2) := \int_0^1 \nabla \mu((1-v)\theta_1 x_1 + v \theta_2 x_2 )dv \)

\section{Upper and lower bounds on the constant \texorpdfstring{$\kappa$}{kappa}}\label{appendix:bounding kappa}

In this appendix, we show the following lemma that bounds $\kappa$ by above and by below. In particular, we recover up to constant factors the bounds proved by \cite{amani2021ucb} for earlier definitions of $\kappa$ (see Appendix~\ref{appendix:previous framework} thereafter).  

\begin{restatable}{lmmnonumber}{} For any even $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathcal{X} = \{x \in \R^d: \|x\| \leq X\}$, we have
\[
      \frac{K}{4} + \frac{K}{4} e^{2SX} \leq \kappa \leq K e^{2SX} \,.
\]
for $\kappa$ as defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:kappa}. 
\end{restatable}

\begin{proof}
We first prove the upper-bound. Fix any \(z\in\R^K\). We bound the second smallest eigenvalue \(\lambda_{K-1}\) of \(\nabla \mu(z)\). using Weyl's inequality \citep{weyl1912asymptotische} and the definition of the gradient of the softmax \( \nabla\mu(z) = \diag(\mu(z)) - \mu(z)\mu(z)^\top \). A direct application of Weyl's inequality gives
\begin{equation*}
    \lambda_{K-1}(\diag(\mu(z)) - \mu(z)\mu(z)^\top) \ge \lambda_K(\diag(\mu(z))) + \lambda_{K-1}( - \mu(z)\mu(z)^\top) = \min_{i\in\llbracket K \rrbracket} \mu(z)_i \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus we have 
\begin{equation*}
    \lambda_{K-1}(\diag(\mu(z)) - \mu(z)\mu(z)^\top) \ge \dfrac{\exp(-S X)}{K \exp(SX)} = \dfrac{1}{K} \exp(-2 SX)
\end{equation*}
where \( X := \max_{x\in\X} \lVert x \rVert_2 \) and \(S\) is assumed such that \( \lVert \theta \rVert_2 \le S \). Hence,
\[
    \kappa := \frac{1}{ \min_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le S} \min_{x\in\X} \lambda_{K-1}(\nabla\mu(\theta x))}  \leq K e^{2SX} \,.
\]

We now prove the lower bound. For simplicity, we assumed that \(\X\) is a ball of radius \(X\) and that \(K\) is even.
A direct application of the Schur-Horn Theorem gives for all \(z\in\R^K\)
\begin{equation*}
    \min_{i,j,i\neq j} \nabla\mu(z)_{ii}+\nabla\mu(z)_{jj} \ge \lambda_{K}(\nabla\mu(z)) + \lambda_{K-1}(\nabla\mu(z)) = \lambda_{K-1}(\nabla\mu(z)) \,.
\end{equation*}
We choose \( \theta \) such that \( \lVert \theta \rVert_2 = S \) and with the first \(K/2\) rows equal to each other, i.e. \( [\theta]_1 = [\theta]_i \) for \(i\in\llbracket K/2 \rrbracket\) and with the others rows collinear in the opposite direction, i.e. \( [\theta]_i = -[\theta]_1 \) for all \(i\ge 2\).
We choose \(x\) such that \( x = -\tfrac{[\theta]_1}{S} X \). Thus we obtain
\begin{multline*}
    \dfrac{4}{K\big(1 + \exp(2SX)\big)} \ge \dfrac{2\exp(-SX)}{\tfrac{K}{2} \exp(-SX) + \tfrac{K}{2} \exp(SX) } \ge \min_{x\in\X}\min_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le S} \min_{i,j,i\neq j} \mu(\theta x)_{ii}+ \mu(\theta x)_{jj} \\
    \ge \min_{x\in\X}\min_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le S} \min_{i,j,i\neq j} \nabla\mu(\theta x)_{ii}+\nabla\mu(\theta x)_{jj} \ge \min_{x\in\X}\min_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le S} \lambda_{K-1}(\nabla\mu(\theta x)) =: \kappa^{-1} \,,
\end{multline*}
which concludes the proof. 
\end{proof}


\section{Comparison with the Framework of \texorpdfstring{\citet{amani2021ucb}}{Amani and Thrampoulidis}}\label{appendix:previous framework}

\citet{amani2021ucb} also consider a MNL bandit framework, which is equivalent but defined slightly differently from ours. 
In their framework, the environment parameter \(\tilde \theta_* \in \R^{K\times d} \) is defined with its last row equal to zero \( [\tilde \theta_*]_K = 0_d \). Therefore the probability of a decision \(i\in\llbracket K \rrbracket\) becomes
\begin{equation*}
    \pr[y_t = i | x_t] = 
    \begin{cases}
        \dfrac{1}{1 + \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} \exp([\tilde\theta_*]_k x_t) } \quad\text{if } i=K \\
        \dfrac{\exp([\tilde \theta_*]_ix_t)}{1+ \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} \exp([\tilde\theta_*]_k x_t) } \quad\text{if } i< K
    \end{cases} \,.
\end{equation*}
The reward vector is also defined \(\tilde \rho\in\R^K_+\) but with its last element equal to zero \( \rho_K = 0 \). The regret is defined as
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde \Reg_T = \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} \tilde\rho_k \left( \pr[y_t = k | x_*] - \pr[y_t = k | x_t] \right) \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus the last element of the probability vector is not needed and we define the vector \( \tilde \mu(\theta x) \in \R^{K-1} \) as the truncated probability vector \( [\tilde \mu(\theta x)]_k = \pr[y_t = k | x_t] \). Contrary to our case, the fact that \(\tilde\mu\) is not a probability ensures that its minimum eigenvalue is well-defined \citep[Lemma~5]{amani2021ucb}. The problem-dependent constant measuring the non-linearity is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
    \tilde \kappa := \dfrac{1}{\min_{x\in\X} \min_{\lVert \theta \rVert_2\le S} \lambda_{\min}(\diag(\tilde\mu(\theta x)) - \tilde\mu(\theta x)\tilde\mu(\theta x)^\top)} \,.
\end{equation*}
As shown by \citep[Eq.~(20)]{amani2021ucb} the constant \(\tilde\kappa\) is exponentially large with respect to \(S\) and \(X\). These lower and upper bounds on \(\tilde\kappa\) show that our constant \(\kappa\) is comparable, see Appendix~\ref{appendix:bounding kappa}.

Now note that in our framework, by choosing without loss of generality \(\min_k \rho_k = \rho_K\) we have
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T &:= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho^\top (\mu(\theta_* x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t)) \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T (\rho - \rho_K 1_K)^\top (\mu(\theta_* x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t)) \\
    &+ \sum_{t=1}^T \rho_K 1_K^\top (\mu(\theta_* x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t)) \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T (\rho - \rho_K 1_K)^\top (\mu(\theta_* x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t)) \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} (\rho_k - \rho_K ) (\mu(\theta_* x_*)_k - \mu(\theta_* x_t)_k)
\end{align*}
We could therefore choose an arbitrary value for \([\theta_*]_K\). For \( [\theta_*]_K = 0_d \) both framework are equivalent. We choose not to truncate the probability vector, as for the proof of our lower-bound having \(\mu(z)\) to be a probability makes the analysis clearer.

\section{Exploration Routine}\label{appendix: exploration routine}

\subsection{Confidence Set}
We build our confidence set over this proposition from \citet[Theorem~1]{zhang2024online}, which is itself an improvement of \citet[Theorem~1]{amani2021ucb}. As demonstrated by \citet[Section~6]{abeille2021instance}, the confidence set presented in the following proposition is not convex. To address this, we construct a convex relaxation, see Proposition~\ref{prop:confidence set after exploring}.

\begin{restatable}{prop}{PropIntermediaryCondidenceSet}\label{prop:exploration first confidence lemma}
    Set the parameter \( \lambda = (S+1) Kd \log(T/\delta) \) with a certain \(\delta \in (0, 1]\). Let the event \(E_\delta\) be defined by 
    \begin{equation*}
        E_\delta : \{\forall t \ge 1, \lVert g_t(\theta_*) - g_t(\hat \theta_{t+1}) \rVert^2_{H_t^{-1}(\theta_*)} \le \gamma_t(\delta) \}
    \end{equation*}
    where \( \gamma_t(\delta) := 16 \lambda \).
    We have that 
    \begin{equation*}
        \pr (E_\delta) \ge 1-\delta\,.
    \end{equation*}
\end{restatable}

Note that \( V_t \preccurlyeq \bar H_t(\theta_*) \) for \( \bar H_t(\theta) := H_t(\theta) + \sum_{s=1}^t \tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K} \otimes x_s x_s^\top \), therefore proving the following lemma is sufficient to prove that 
\begin{equation*}
    \pr( \theta_* \in \Theta) \ge 1 - \delta \,.
\end{equation*}

\begin{restatable}{prop}{PropConfidenceSetAfterExploring}\label{prop:confidence set after exploring}
    Let \(\delta\in(0,1]\) and \(\hat \theta_{t+1}\) be defined as in Algorithm~\ref{algo:exploration routine}. We have that 
    \begin{equation*}
        \pr\left(\forall t\ge 1, \lVert\hat\theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{\bar H_t(\theta_*)} \le \beta_t(\delta)\right) \ge 1-\delta 
    \end{equation*}
    where \( \bar H_t(\theta) := H_t(\theta) + \sum_{s=1}^t \tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K} \otimes x_s x_s^\top \) and \(\beta_t(\delta) := \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right)^2 \gamma_t(\delta)\) with \(\gamma_t(\delta)\) and \(\lambda\) defined in Proposition~\ref{prop:exploration first confidence lemma}.
\end{restatable}

We follow the proof of Lemma~1 in \citet{faury2022jointly}.
\begin{proof}
\textbf{Step 1: Sub-Exponential Self-Concordance.}

We first show that for all time step \(t\ge 1\), if the event \(E_\delta\) holds, we have that
\begin{equation*}
    H_t(\theta_*) \preccurlyeq \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right) G_t(\theta_*, \hat \theta_{t+1})
\end{equation*}
where \(\lambda\) and \(\gamma_t(\delta)\) are defined in Proposition~\ref{prop:exploration first confidence lemma}.
From the proof of Lemma~13 in \citet{amani2021ucb} we have that
\begin{equation*}
    H_t(\theta_*) \preccurlyeq \sum_{s=1}^t (1+d(x_s, \hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)) \alpha_s(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*) + \lambda I_{Kd}
\end{equation*}
where \( d(x_s, \hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*) := \lVert (\hat\theta_{t+1} - \theta_*)x_s\rVert_2 \). From now on the proof of Lemma~2 of \citet{abeille2021instance} also holds in the multiclass setting to conclude this proof step. We provide it for the sake of completeness. We apply Cauchy-Schwartz inequality and obtain
\begin{multline*}
    d(x_s, \hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*) \le \lVert x_s \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \lVert \hat\theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert_{G_t(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \\ \le \lVert x_s \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \le \lambda^{-1/2} \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \,.
\end{multline*}
Putting it back we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sub_exp_self_concordance eq1}
    H_t(\theta_*) \preccurlyeq \left(1+ \lambda^{-1/2} \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \right) G_t(\theta_*, \hat\theta_{t+1})\,.
\end{equation}
Therefore using this matrix inequality and event \(E_\delta\) we get
\begin{align*}
    \lVert g_t(\hat \theta_{t+1}) &- g_t(\theta_*) \rVert^2_{G_t^{-1}(\theta_*, \hat\theta_{t+1})} \\
    &\le \left( 1+ \lambda^{-1/2} \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \right) \lVert g_t(\hat \theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert^2_{H_t^{-1}(\theta_*)} \\
    &\le \gamma_t(\delta) \lambda^{-1/2} \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} + \gamma_t(\delta) \,.
\end{align*}
Solving for \(\lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)}\) we get 
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) - g_t(\theta_*) \rVert_{G_t^{-1}(\hat \theta_{t+1}, \theta_*)} \le \gamma_t(\delta) \lambda^{-1/2} + \sqrt{\gamma_t(\delta)}\,.
\end{equation*}
We now put this back in Eq.\eqref{eq:sub_exp_self_concordance eq1} to conclude and obtain:
\begin{equation*}
    H_t(\theta_*) \preccurlyeq \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right) G_t(\theta_*, \hat \theta_{t+1}) \,.
\end{equation*}

\textbf{Step 2: Applying Self-concordance.}

We apply twice the self-concordance property to get
\begin{align*}
    \lVert \theta_* - \hat\theta_{t+1}\rVert^2_{H_t(\theta_*)} &\le \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right) \lVert \theta_* - \hat\theta_{t+1}\rVert^2_{G_t(\theta_*, \hat\theta_{t+1})} \\
    &\le \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right) \lVert g_t(\theta_*) - g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) \rVert^2_{G_t^{-1}(\theta_*, \hat\theta_{t+1})} \\
    &\le \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right)^2 \lVert g_t(\theta_*) - g_t(\hat\theta_{t+1}) \rVert^2_{H_t^{-1}(\theta_*)} \\
    &\le \left(1 + \dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda} + \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma_t(\delta)}{\lambda}} \right)^2 \gamma_t(\delta) \\
    &=: \beta_t(\delta) \,.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 3: From \(H_t(\theta_*)\) to \(\bar H_t(\theta_*)\).}

We decompose \(\R^K\) as \( \R^K = 1_K \oplus \calH \) where \(\calH\) is the hyperplane supported by \(1_K\). Recall that \(\theta_* \in \Pi R^{K\times d} \) and \(\hat \theta_{t+1}\in\Pi\R^{K\times d} \), for all \(x\in \X\), by definition of \(\Pi\), \( \theta_* x \) and \( \hat \theta_{t+1} x \) are in \(\calH\). Therefore \( \sum_{s=1}^t \lVert (\theta_* - \hat \theta_{t+1})x_s \rVert^2_{\tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K}} = 0 \). And we can conclude by
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_* - \hat\theta_{t+1}\rVert^2_{\bar H_t(\theta_*)} = \lVert \theta_* - \hat\theta_{t+1}\rVert^2_{H_t(\theta_*)} \le \beta_t(\delta) \,.
\end{equation*}

\end{proof}

\subsection{Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:constant diameter}}\label{appendix:proof constant diameter}
\LmmConstantDiameter*
We adapt the proof of Lemma~2 of \citet{faury2022jointly} to the multiclass setting.
\begin{proof}
We start by making the term \(I_K\) appear in order to match the dimension of \(\bar H_t(\theta_*)\).
\begin{align*}
    \diam(\Theta) &= \max_{x\in\X}\max_{\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta} \lVert (\theta_1 - \theta_2) x \rVert_2 \\
    &= \max_{x\in\X}\max_{\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta} \lVert (I_K \otimes x^\top ) (\theta_1 - \theta_2) \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \max_{x\in\X}\max_{\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta} \lVert I_K \otimes x^\top \rVert_{V_\tau^{-1}} \lVert \theta_1 - \theta_2\rVert_{V_\tau} && \text{Cauchy-Schwartz} \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \max_{x\in\X} \lVert I_K \otimes x \rVert_{V_\tau^{-1}} && \text{Proposition~\ref{prop:confidence set after exploring} and symmetry} \\
    &= 2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \sqrt{\max_{x\in\X} \lVert I_K \otimes x \rVert^2_{V_\tau^{-1}}} \\
    &= 2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \tau^{-1/2} \sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^\tau \max_{x\in\X} \lVert I_K \otimes x \rVert^2_{V_\tau^{-1}}} \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \tau^{-1/2} \sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^\tau \max_{x\in\X} \lVert I_K \otimes x \rVert^2_{V_{s-1}^{-1}}} && (V_\tau \succcurlyeq V_{s-1}) \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \tau^{-1/2} \sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^\tau \lVert I_K \otimes x_s \rVert^2_{V_{s-1}^{-1}}} && \text{definition of \(x_s\)} \\
    &=2 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \tau^{-1/2} \kappa^{1/2} \sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^\tau \lVert \kappa^{-1/2} I_K \otimes x_s \rVert^2_{V_{s-1}^{-1}}} \\
    &\le4 \sqrt{\beta_\tau(\delta)} \tau^{-1/2} \kappa^{1/2} \sqrt{Kd \log\left(1+\tfrac{\tau}{Kd}\right)} && \text{\citet[lemma~10]{abbasi2011improved}}
\end{align*}
Thus if we choose \(\tau = 16 \beta_\tau(\delta)\kappa Kd\log\left(1+\tfrac{T}{Kd}\right) \) we have that \( \diam(\Theta) \le 1 \).
\end{proof}


\section{Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:confidence set learning}}\label{appendix:proof confidence set learning}

\LmmConfidenceSetLearning*
\begin{proof}
Throughout the proof we assume that \(\diam(\Theta) \le 1\), which is verified with probability \(1-\delta\) thanks to Lemma~\ref{lemma:constant diameter}. We apply a Union Bound at the end.

\textbf{Step 1: Decomposition.}

Combining \citep[Lemma~8]{abeille2021instance} and \citep[Corollary~2]{sun2019generalized} we obtain for all \(t\ge 1\) and all \(\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta \)
\begin{equation*}
    \tilde \alpha_t(\theta_1, \theta_2) \succcurlyeq \dfrac{1}{2+\diam(\Theta)} \nabla \mu(\theta_2 x_t) \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus using a Taylor expansion with integral remainder we get
\begin{equation*}
    \ell_{t+1}(\theta_1) \ge \ell_{t+1}(\theta_2) + \langle \nabla \ell_{t+1}(\theta_2), \theta_1 - \theta_2 \rangle + \dfrac{1}{2+\diam(\Theta)} \lVert \theta_1 - \theta_2 \rVert_{\nabla^2 \ell_{t+1}(\theta_2)} \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus by rearranging 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:learning confidence eq 1}
    \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) \le \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rangle - \dfrac{1}{3} \lVert (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) x_s \rVert^2_{\nabla\mu(\theta_{s+1}x_s)} \,.
\end{equation}
Recall that we define \(\theta_{s+1} \) by
\begin{equation*}
    \theta_{s+1} := \argmin_{\theta\in\Theta} \left( \dfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \theta - \theta'_s \rVert^2_{W_s} + \ell_{s+1}(\theta) =: \tilde L_{s+1}(\theta) \right) \,.
\end{equation*}
Note that the objective function \(\tilde L_{s+1}\) is convex and the set \(\Theta\) is convex, therefore for all \(\theta \in \Theta\),
\begin{align*}
    \langle\nabla\tilde L_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta - \theta_{s+1} \rangle &\ge 0 \\
    \dfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \langle\theta_{s+1} - \theta_s', W_s (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) \rangle &\ge \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rangle \,.
\end{align*}
Using this inequality in Eq.~\eqref{eq:learning confidence eq 1} we get
\begin{align*}
    \tfrac{3}{2}&\left(\ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*)\right) \\
    &\le \exp(-\sqrt{6}) \langle\theta_{s+1} - \theta_s', W_s (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) \rangle - \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) x_s \rVert^2_{\nabla\mu(\theta_{s+1}x_s)} \\
    &= \tfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{2} \left[ -\lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} + \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} - \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{W_s} \right] - \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) x_s \rVert^2_{\nabla\mu(\theta_{s+1}x_s)} \\
    &\le \tfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{2} \left[ -\lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} + \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} \right] - \tfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{2} \lVert (\theta_* - \theta_{s+1}) x_s \rVert^2_{\nabla\mu(\theta_{s+1}'x_s)} \,.
\end{align*}
We regroup the terms and apply the triangular inequality
\begin{align*}
    \tfrac{3\exp(\sqrt{6})}{2}&\left(\ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*)\right) \\
    &\le -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{s+1}} +\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} \\
    &\le -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{s+1}} +\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} +\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert^2_{W_s} + \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert_{W_s} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert_{W_s} \\
    &\le -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{s+1}} +\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} + \tfrac{1}{2}(s+\lambda)\epsilon_s^2 + (s + \lambda) \lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \epsilon_s
\end{align*}
where the last inequality is due to 
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert_{W_s} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert_{W_s} \le \lambda_{\max}(W_s) \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert_2 \, \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert_2 \le (s+\lambda) \lVert V_\tau^{-1/2} \rVert_2 \, \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert_{V_\tau} \epsilon_s
\end{equation*}
and \( \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert^2_{W_s} \le \lambda_{\max} (W_s) \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_s \rVert_2^2 \le (s+\lambda)\epsilon_s^2 \) since \(\lambda_{\max}(W_s)\le s+\lambda \). By summing we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \tfrac{3\exp(\sqrt{6})}{2} &\sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) \\
    &\le \sum_{s=1}^t -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{s+1}} +\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_s} + \tfrac{s+\lambda}{2}\epsilon_s^2 + (s+\lambda)\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \epsilon_s \\
    &= -\tfrac{1}{2}\lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} + \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_1 - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_1} + \sum_{s=1}^t \tfrac{s+\lambda}{2}\epsilon_s^2 + (s+\lambda)\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \epsilon_s \\
    &= -\tfrac{1}{2}\lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} + 2 \beta_\tau(\delta) + \sum_{s=1}^t \tfrac{s+\lambda}{2}\epsilon_s^2 + (s+\lambda)\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \epsilon_s 
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we use \(  \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_1 - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_1} = \tfrac{\lambda}{2} \lVert \theta_1 - \theta_* \rVert^2_2 \le \tfrac{\lambda}{2} \lVert V_\tau^{-1}\rVert_2 . \lVert  \theta_1 - \theta_* \rVert^2_{V_\tau} \le 2 \beta_\tau(\delta) \).
We rearrange the terms:
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le 2\beta_\tau(\delta) +  \sum_{s=1}^t (s+\lambda)(\epsilon_s^2+ 2\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \epsilon_s) + 3 \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \,.
\end{equation*}
Using the triangle and Young's inequalities we have that
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta'_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le 2\lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} + 2\lVert \theta'_{t+1} - \theta_{t+1} \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le 2\lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} + 2(t+1+\lambda)\epsilon_{t+1}^2 \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus we have
%\begin{multline*}
%    \lVert \theta'_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \\
%    \le 4\beta_\tau(\delta) + 2 \sum_{s=1}^{t+1} (s+\lambda)\epsilon_s^2 + 4\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \sum_{s=1}^t (s+\lambda) \epsilon_s + 6 \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \,.
%\end{multline*}
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta'_{t+1} - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}}
    \le 4\beta_\tau(\delta) + 2 \sum_{s=1}^{t+1} (s+\lambda)\epsilon_s^2 + 4\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \sum_{s=1}^t (s+\lambda) \epsilon_s + 6 \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \,.
\end{equation*}
The two first sums can be bounded by choosing \(\epsilon_s = s^{-2}\). To bound the last term we introduce a new term 
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) = \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) + \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1})
\end{equation*}
with \(\bar \theta_s\) defined by
\begin{equation*}
    \bar \theta_s := \argmin_{\theta\in\Theta} \dfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \theta - \theta'_s \rVert^2_{W_s} + \sum_{k=1}^K \ell(\theta x_s, k) + \langle \underbrace{(\mathbbm{1}_K - K \mu(\theta_s x_s) ) \otimes x_s}_{\text{linear bias}}, \theta \rangle \,.
\end{equation*}
Note that \(\bar\theta_s\) is \(\F_s\) measurable while \( \theta_{s+1} \) is \(\F_{s+1}\) measurable. This estimator \(\bar\theta_s\) is inspired by the work of \citet{agarwal2022efficient} in the full information setting. We tailor their work to our needs by performing the optimisation over \(\Theta\) instead of \( \R^{K\times d} \), modifying the linear bias and adapting it as an Online Mirror Descent algorithm.


\textbf{Step 2: Bounding the first sum.}

In this step we bound the term \( \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) \). Using Eq.~\eqref{eq:learning confidence eq 1} with \(\theta_*\) and \(\bar\theta_s\) we get
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) &\le \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*), \theta_* - \bar\theta_s \rangle - \tfrac{1}{3} \lVert \theta_* - \bar \theta_s \rVert_{\nabla\ell_{s+1}(\theta_*)} \\
    &= \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \mu(\theta_*x_s)-e_{y_s}, \phi_s \rangle - \tfrac{1}{3} \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_s) \phi_s, \phi_s \rangle \\
    &= \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \epsilon_{s+1}, \phi_s \rangle - \tfrac{1}{3} \Phi_t
\end{align*}
where \(\epsilon_{s+1}:= \mu(\theta_*x_s)-e_{y_s} \), \( \phi_s := (\theta_* - \bar\theta_s)x_s \) and \( \smash{\Phi_t := \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_s) \phi_s, \phi_s \rangle} \). We have that \( \E[ \langle \epsilon_{s+1}, \phi_s \rangle^2 | \F_s ] = \langle \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_s) \phi_s, \phi_s \rangle \) and using Cauchy-Schwartz inequality \( | \langle \epsilon_{s+1}, \phi_s \rangle | \le 2 \). We apply Lemma~\ref{lemma:modified Freedman inequality} and get
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \langle \epsilon_{s+1}, \phi_s \rangle \le (e-2) \eta \Phi_t + \tfrac{1}{\eta} \log \delta^{-1} \quad w.p. \; 1-\delta
\end{equation*}
where \(\delta\in(0,1]\) and \(\eta\in[0, 1/2]\). Thus we have
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) \le (e-2) \eta \Phi_t - \tfrac{1}{3} \Phi_t + \tfrac{1}{\eta} \log \delta^{-1} \quad w.p.\; 1-\delta \,.
\end{equation*}
We choose \(\eta = \tfrac{1}{3(e-2)} \) which verifies \(\eta\le1/2\). Thus, this gives probability $1-\delta$
 \[
  \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\theta_*) - \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) \leq 3(e-2) \log \delta^{-1}\,.
 \]


\textbf{Step 3: Bounding the second sum.}
\nopagebreak

In this step we bound the term \( \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \). Note that \(\bar \theta_s \) is defined as the minimiser of a convex objective function over the convex set \(\Theta\). Since \(\theta_{s+1}\in\Theta\), applying Lemma~\ref{lemma:minimiser to gradient positive} we have
\begin{align*}
    0&\le \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \langle\bar \theta_s - \theta'_s, W_s(\theta_{s+1}-\bar\theta_s)\rangle \\
    &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^K \langle \nabla\ell(\bar\theta_s x_s, k), \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle + \langle (\mathbbm{1}_K - K \mu(\theta_s x_s) ) \otimes x_s, \theta_{s+1} - \bar\theta_s \rangle \\
    &\le \tfrac{-2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{W_s} + \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \langle \theta_{s+1} - \theta'_s, W_s (\theta_{s+1} -\bar \theta_s)\rangle \\
    &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^K \langle \nabla\ell(\bar\theta_s x_s, k), \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle + \langle (\mathbbm{1}_K - K \mu(\theta_s x_s) ) \otimes x_s, \theta_{s+1} - \bar\theta_s \rangle \,.
\end{align*}
Using the same reasoning for \(\theta_{s+1}\) we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \langle \theta_{s+1} - \theta'_s, W_s (\theta_{s+1} -\bar \theta_s)\rangle \le \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \bar \theta_{s}-\theta_{s+1} \rangle \,.
\end{equation*}
Combining both inequalities we get
\begin{multline*}
    0\le \tfrac{-2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{W_s} + \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \bar \theta_{s}-\theta_{s+1} \rangle \\
    + \sum_{k=1}^K \langle \nabla\ell(\bar\theta_s x_s, k), \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle +  \langle (\mathbbm{1}_K - K \mu(\theta_s x_s) ) \otimes x_s, \theta_{s+1} - \bar\theta_s \rangle \,.
\end{multline*}
Rearranging and using the Mean-value Theorem we get
\begin{align*}
    0 &\le \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) - \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) , \bar \theta_{s} - \theta_{s+1} \rangle \\
    &\qquad + \left\langle \sum_{k=1}^K \nabla\ell(\bar\theta_s x_s, k) + (\mathbbm{1}_K - K \mu(\theta_s x_s) ) \otimes x_s - \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s), \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \right\rangle \\
    0 &\le \langle \alpha_s(\theta_{s+1}, \bar\theta_s) (\theta_{s+1} - \bar\theta_s), \bar \theta_{s} - \theta_{s+1} \rangle + \langle K(\mu(\bar\theta_s x_s) - \mu(\theta_s x_s)) \otimes x_s -\nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle \\
    0 &\le -\lVert \theta_{s+1} - \bar\theta_s \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\theta_{s+1}, \bar\theta_s)} + K \langle \alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s) (\bar\theta_s-\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle - \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle \\
    0 &\le K \langle \alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s) (\bar\theta_s-\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle - \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle \,.
\end{align*}
We use the following decomposition
%\begin{multline*}
%    \langle \alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s) (\bar\theta_s-\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle \\
%    = -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_s \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \,.
%\end{multline*}
\begin{equation*}
    \langle \alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s) (\bar\theta_s-\theta_s) , \theta_{s+1} - \bar \theta_s \rangle 
    = -\tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert \bar \theta_s - \theta_s \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \,.
\end{equation*}
We apply the triangular inequality on the second term and get
%\begin{align*}
%    \lVert \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} &\le \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + \lVert \theta_s - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \\
%    &\le \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + s \epsilon_s^2 \,.
%\end{align*}
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \le \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + \lVert \theta_s - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \le \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} + s \epsilon_s^2 \,.
\end{equation*}
We first bound \( \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{W_s} \). Recall that \( \langle \nabla \tilde L_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta - \theta_{s+1} \rangle \ge 0 \) for all \( \theta \in \Theta \). Choosing \(\theta = \theta_s'\) we get
%\begin{align*}
%    \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{W_s} &\le \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rangle \\
%    &\le \lVert \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \rVert_{W_s^{-1}} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert_{W_s}\,.
%\end{align*}
\begin{equation*}
    \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{W_s} \le \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}), \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rangle \le \lVert \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \rVert_{W_s^{-1}} \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert_{W_s}\,.
\end{equation*}
Dividing by \( \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert_{W_s} \) gives
\begin{align*}
    \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert_{W_s} &\le \lVert \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \rVert_{W_s^{-1}} \\
    &\le \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda}} \lVert \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda}} \lVert (\mu(\theta_{s+1} x_s) - e_{y_s}) \otimes x_s \rVert_2 \\
    &= \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda}} \lVert (\mu(\theta_{s+1} x_s) - e_{y_s}) \rVert_2 \lVert x_s \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda}} \lVert (\mu(\theta_{s+1} x_s) - e_{y_s}) \rVert_1 && (\lVert x \rVert_2 \le 1, \forall x \in \X) \\
    &\le \tfrac{2}{\sqrt{\lambda}} \,. &&\text{(Triangular Inequality)}
\end{align*}
Using this result we bound \( \lVert \theta_s' - \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \).
\begin{align*}
    \lVert \theta_s' &- \theta_{s+1} \rVert^2_{\alpha_s(\bar\theta_s, \theta_s)} \\
    &= \left\lVert \left[ \int_0^1 \nabla\mu(\bar\theta_s x_s + v(\theta_s - \bar \theta_s)x_s)dv \right]^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) (\theta_{s+1} - \theta_s') \right\rVert_2^2 \\
    &\le \left\lVert \left[ \int_0^1 \nabla\mu(\bar\theta_s x_s + v(\theta_s - \bar \theta_s)x_s)dv \right]^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \right\rVert_2^2 \lVert \theta_{s+1} - \theta_s' \rVert^2_{W_s} \\
    &\le 9 \exp(2\sqrt{6}) \tfrac{1}{\lambda} \left\lVert \left[ \int_0^1 \nabla\mu(\bar\theta_s x_s + v(\theta_s - \bar \theta_s)x_s)dv \right]^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \right\rVert_2^2 \\
    &\le 9 \exp(3\sqrt{6}) \tfrac{1}{\lambda} \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \rVert_2^2
\end{align*}
where the last inequality is by self-concordance and convexity of \(\Theta\).
We rearrange the terms to get
\begin{equation*}
    \langle \nabla\ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s) , \bar \theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rangle \le K \tfrac{9}{2} \exp(3\sqrt{6}) \tfrac{1}{\lambda} \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \rVert_2^2 + Ks\epsilon_s^2 \,.
\end{equation*}
As \(\ell_{s+1} \) is a convex function we have that
\begin{align*}
    \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) &\le \langle \nabla \ell_{s+1}(\bar\theta_s), \bar\theta_s - \theta_{s+1} \rangle\\
    &\le K \tfrac{9}{2} \exp(\sqrt{6}) \tfrac{1}{\lambda} \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \rVert^2_2 + Ks\epsilon_s^2 \,.
\end{align*}
Let us bound the sum using \citep[Lemma~19]{zhang2024online}, we provide the proof for the sake of completeness. We have
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t &\lVert \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \rVert^2_2 \\
    &\le \sum_{s=1}^t \lambda_{\max}\left(\left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} \otimes x_s^\top \right) W_s^{-1} \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} \otimes x_s \right)\right) \\
    &= \sum_{s=1}^t \lambda_{\max}\left(\left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top \right) W_s^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le \sum_{s=1}^t \Tr\left(\left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top \right) W_s^{-1} \right) \,.
\end{align*}
Let us define \( M_s := \sum_{r=1}^s \nabla\mu(\theta'_{r+1}x_r) \otimes x_r x_r^\top + \lambda I_{Kd} \). For \(\lambda\ge2\) we have that \( M_s \preccurlyeq W_s \). This gives us
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s)^{1/2} (I_K \otimes x_s^\top) W_s^{-1/2} \rVert^2_2 &\le \sum_{s=1}^t \Tr((M_s-M_{s-1})M_s^{-1}) \\
    &\le \sum_{s=1}^t \log \dfrac{|M_s|}{|M_{s-1}|} && \text{\citep[Lemma~4.5]{hazan2016introduction}} \\
    &\le Kd \log\left( 1 + \dfrac{tL}{\lambda Kd} \right) \,.
\end{align*}

Therefore
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{s=1}^t \ell_{s+1}(\bar \theta_s) - \ell_{s+1}(\theta_{s+1}) \le K \sum_{s=1}^t s \epsilon_s^2 + \dfrac{9}{2\lambda} \exp{\sqrt{6}} K^2d \log\left( 1 + \dfrac{tL}{\lambda K d} \right).
\end{equation*}

\textbf{Step 4: Putting everything together.}
\nopagebreak

Applying a Union Bound with for Lemma~\ref{lemma:constant diameter}, we obtain that with probability \(1-2\delta\)
\begin{multline}
    \lVert \theta_{t+1}' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le 4\beta_\tau(\delta) + 2 \sum_{s=1}^{t+1} (s+\lambda)\epsilon_s^2 + 4\lambda^{-1/2} \beta_\tau(\delta)^{1/2} \sum_{s=1}^t (s+\lambda)\epsilon_s \\
    + 27 \exp(3\sqrt{6})\lambda^{-1} K^2 d \log\left( 1 + \dfrac{tL}{\lambda Kd} \right) + 18(e-2)\log \delta^{-1}  \,.
\end{multline}
Substituting \(\epsilon_s = s^{-2}\) and \( \lambda = (S+1) Kd \log(T/\delta) \), this may be further upper-bounded for some universal constant $\cste >0$ as
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_{t+1}' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le \cste (S+1) Kd \log(T/\delta) =:  \sigma_t(\delta)
\end{equation*}

\textbf{Step 5: From \(W_{t+1}\) to \(\bar W_{t+1}\).}

We decompose \(\R^K\) as \( \R^K = 1_K \oplus \calH \) where \(\calH\) is the hyperplane supported by \(1_K\). Recall that \(\theta_*, \hat \theta_{t+1} \in \Pi \R^{K\times d} \), for all \(x\in\X\), by definition of \(\Pi\), \(\theta_{t+1}' x\) and \( \theta_* x \) are in \(\calH\). Therefore \(  \sum_{s=1}^t \lVert (\theta_{t+1}' - \theta_*)x_s \rVert^2_{\tfrac{1_K 1_K^\top}{K}} = 0 \). And we conclude that with probability \(1-2\delta\)
\begin{equation*}
    \lVert \theta_{t+1}' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{\bar W_{t+1}} = \lVert \theta_{t+1}' - \theta_* \rVert^2_{W_{t+1}} \le \sigma_t(\delta) \,.
\end{equation*}

\end{proof}

\section{Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:regret bound}}\label{appendix:proof thm regret bound}
\ThmRegretBound*
\begin{proof}
Throughout the proof we assume that
\begin{equation*}
    \diam(\Theta) \le 1
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
    \forall t\ge1, \lVert \theta_* - \theta'_{t+1} \rVert^2_{\bar W_{t+1}} \le \sigma_t(\delta)
\end{equation*}
which is verified with probability \(1-2\delta\) thanks to Lemma~\ref{lemma:constant diameter} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:confidence set learning}, we apply a Union Bound at the end. 
The regret of the exploration phase is smaller than
\begin{equation*}
    \tau \le \cste K^{3/2} d^{3/2} \kappa \log^{3/2}(T) \,.
\end{equation*}
Let us now focus on the second phase of the algorithm.

\textbf{Step 1: Using optimism.}

Using the definition of the optimistic reward we can bound the regret twice. 
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\mathrm{Learning}) &:= \sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \rho^\top (\mu(\theta_*x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t)) \\
    &\le \sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \rho^\top \mu(\theta'_t x_*) + \epsilon_{1,t}(x_*) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_*) - \rho^\top \mu(\theta_* x_t) && \text{(Prop.~\ref{prop:optimistic reward})} \\
    &\le \sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \rho^\top \mu(\theta'_t x_t) + \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) - \rho^\top \mu(\theta_* x_t) &&\text{(Def. of \(x_t\))} \\
    &\le 2 \sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + 2 \sum_{t=\tau+1}^T \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) &&\text{(Prop.~\ref{prop:optimistic reward})} \\
    &\le 2 \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + 2 \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 2: Bounding the sum of \(\epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) \).}
\nopagebreak

We start by bounding the second sum
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) &= 3 \sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_t(\delta) \lVert (I_K \otimes x_t^\top) \bar W_t^{-1/2} \rVert_2^2 \\
    &\le 3 \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert (I_K \otimes x_t^\top) \bar W_t^{-1/2} \rVert_2^2 \\
    &= 3 \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bar W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \rVert_2^2 \\
    &\le 3 \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \lambda_{\max} \left( (I_K \otimes x_t^\top) \bar W_t^{-1} (I_K \otimes x_t) \right) \\ 
    &= 3 \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \lambda_{\max} \left( \left(I_K \otimes x_t x_t^\top\right) \bar W_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le 3 \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr\left( \left(I_K \otimes x_t x_t^\top\right) \bar W_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &= 3 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr\left( \left( \tfrac{1}{\kappa} I_K \otimes x_t x_t^\top\right) \bar W_t^{-1} \right) \,.
\end{align*}
Let us define \( U_t := \sum_{s=1}^t \tfrac{1}{\kappa} I_K \otimes x_s x_s^\top +\tfrac{\lambda}{2} I_{Kd} \). We have that \( U_t \preccurlyeq \bar W_t \) for \(\lambda \ge 2\). We have that 
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) &\le 3 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr\left( ( U_t - U_{t-1} ) U_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le 3 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) \sum_{t=1}^T \log \dfrac{|U_t|}{|U_{t-1}|} &&\text{\citep[Lemma~4.5]{hazan2016introduction}} \\
    &\le 3 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) Kd \log\left( 1+ \dfrac{T}{Kd\lambda\kappa} \right)\,. &&\text{(Lemma~\ref{lemma:det_trace inequality})}
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 3: Decomposing the sum of \(\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) \).}

Let us now focus on the first sum.
\small
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T &\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) \\
    &:= \sum_{t=1}^T \sqrt{\sigma_t(\delta)} \lVert \bar W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t) \rho \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \sqrt{\sigma_t(\delta)} \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t) \rho \rVert_2 &&(\bar W_{t+1}^{-1} \preccurlyeq W_{t+1}^{-1}) \\
    &\le \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t) \rho \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_t)^{1/2} \rho \rVert_2 &&\text{(Self-concordance)} \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \rVert_2 \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_t)^{1/2} \rho \rVert_2 \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \rVert_2^2} \sqrt{ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_t)^{1/2} \rho \rVert_2^2} \,. &&\text{(Cauchy-Schwartz)}
\end{align*}
\normalsize
Once again we have two separate terms to bound. We start with the left term.

\textbf{Step 4: Bounding the sum of \(\lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \rVert_2^2\).}

\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T &\lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \rVert_2^2 \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \lambda_{\max} \left( \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \otimes x_t^\top \right) W_t^{-1} \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \otimes x_t \right) \right) \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \lambda_{\max} \left( \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t) \otimes x_t x_t^\top \right) W_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr \left( \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t) \otimes x_t x_t^\top \right) W_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr \left( \left( \nabla\mu(\theta'_{t+1} x_t) \otimes x_t x_t^\top \right) W_t^{-1} \right)
\end{align*}
where the last inequality is due to self-concordance.
Now that we have applied the self-concordance property, we may apply \citep[Lemma~19]{zhang2024online}. We provide the proof for the sake of completeness.
Let us define \( M_t := \sum_{s=1}^t \nabla\mu(\theta'_{s+1} x_s) \otimes x_s x_s^\top + \tfrac{\lambda}{2} I_{Kd} \). We have that \( M_t \preccurlyeq W_t \) when \(\lambda\ge2\). We obtain
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert W_t^{-1/2} (I_K \otimes x_t) \nabla\mu(\theta'_t x_t)^{1/2} \rVert_2^2 &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sum_{t=1}^T \Tr \left( \left( M_t - M_{t-1} \right) M_t^{-1} \right) \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sum_{t=1}^T \log \dfrac{|M_t|}{|M_{t-1}|} &&\text{\citep[Lemma~4.5]{hazan2016introduction}} \\
    &\le \exp(\sqrt{6}) Kd \log\left( 1+ \dfrac{TL}{\lambda Kd} \right) \,. &&\text{(Lemma~\ref{lemma:det_trace inequality})}
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 5: Bounding the sum of \(\lVert \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_t)^{1/2} \rho \rVert_2^2\).}

We add and subtract a term and get
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T &\lVert \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_t)^{1/2} \rho \rVert_2^2 \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, \nabla\mu(\theta_*x_*)\rho\rangle + \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, (\nabla\mu(\theta_*x_t) - \nabla\mu(\theta_*x_*)) \rho \rangle \\
    &\le T / \kappa_* + \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, (\nabla\mu(\theta_*x_t) - \nabla\mu(\theta_*x_*)) \rho \rangle \,.
\end{align*}
We use the definition of \(\nabla\mu(.)\) and get
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T &\langle \rho, (\nabla\mu(\theta_*x_t) - \nabla\mu(\theta_*x_*)) \rho \rangle \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, \diag(\mu(\theta_* x_t) - \mu(\theta_*x_*)) \rho \rangle + \langle \rho, (\mu(\theta_*x_*) \mu(\theta_*x_*)^\top - \mu(\theta_*x_t) \mu(\theta_*x_t)^\top ) \rho \rangle \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, 2(\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) \mathbbm{1}_K \rangle + \langle \rho, \mu(\theta_* x_*) \rangle^2 - \langle \rho, \mu(\theta_*x_t)\rangle^2 \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{K} \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) + \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \rho, \mu(\theta_*x_*) - \mu(\theta_* x_t) \rangle \langle\rho, \mu(\theta_*x_*)+\mu(\theta_*x_t)\rangle \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{K} \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) + 2 \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) \langle\rho, \mu(\theta_*x_*)+\mu(\theta_*x_t)\rangle \\
    &\le 2 \sqrt{K} \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) + 4 \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t)) \\
    &= (2\sqrt{K}+4) \sum_{t=1}^T (\epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t))
\end{align*}
where the first and third inequalities are by Proposition~\ref{prop:optimistic reward}, the second and fourth inequalities are due to the Cauchy-Schwartz inequality.

\textbf{Step 6: Putting everything together.}

Combining our previous results we get
\small
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\mathrm{Learning}) \le &2 \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) \\
    \le &6 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) Kd \log\left(1 + \tfrac{T}{Kd\lambda \kappa} \right) \\
    &+\exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \left[ \exp(\sqrt{6}) Kd \log\left(1+ \tfrac{TL}{\lambda Kd}\right) \right]^{1/2} \left[ \tfrac{T}{\kappa_*} + (2\sqrt{K} + 4) \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) \right]^{1/2} \\
    \le &6 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) Kd \log\left(1 + \tfrac{T}{Kd\lambda \kappa} \right) \\
    &+\exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \left[ \exp(\sqrt{6}) Kd \log\left(1+ \tfrac{TL}{\lambda Kd}\right) \right]^{1/2} \sqrt{ \tfrac{T}{\kappa_*} } \\
    &+ \exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \left[ \exp(\sqrt{6}) Kd \log\left(1+ \tfrac{TL}{\lambda Kd}\right) \right]^{1/2} \left[ (2\sqrt{K} + 4) \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) \right]^{1/2} \,.
\end{align*}
\normalsize
We use the fact that \( x^2 - bx -c \le 0 \implies x^2 \le 2b^2 + 2c \) with \( x^2 =\sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_{1,t}(x_t) + \epsilon_{2,t}(x_t) \) and get with probability \( 1-2\delta \)
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\mathrm{Learning}) \le &6 \kappa \sigma_T(\delta) Kd \log\left(1 + \tfrac{T}{Kd\lambda \kappa} \right) \\
    &+\exp(\sqrt{6}) \sqrt{\sigma_T(\delta)} \left[ \exp(\sqrt{6}) Kd \log\left(1+ \tfrac{TL}{\lambda Kd}\right) \right]^{1/2} \sqrt{ \tfrac{T}{\kappa_*} } \\
    &+\exp(3\sqrt{6}) \sigma_T(\delta) (2\sqrt{K} + 4)  Kd \log\left(1+ \tfrac{TL}{\lambda K d} \right) \\
    \le &\cste (S+1)^{1/2} K d \log(T/\delta) \sqrt{T/\kappa_*} + \cste (S+1) \kappa K^{5/2} d^{2} \log^2(T/\delta) \,.
\end{align*}
where applying the Union Bound gives the result with probability \(1-2\delta\).

\end{proof}

\section{Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:lower bound}}\label{appendix:proof lower bound}
\ThmLowerBound*

\begin{proof}
We adapt the proof of \citet[Theorem~2]{abeille2021instance} to the multiclass setting.
We fix an algorithm \(\pi\). We use the canonical bandit probability space \( (\Omega_t, \F_t, \pr_{\pi \theta \rho}) \) of \citet[Section~4.7]{lattimore2020bandit}. To simplify let us denote \( \pr_\theta = \pr_{\pi \theta \rho} \) the probability of the random sequence \( \{x_1, y_1, \dots , x_T, y_T \} \) obtained by having the algorithm \(\pi\) interact with the environment \((\theta, \rho)\). The expectation \(\E_\theta\) is computed with respect to the probability \(\pr_\theta\).

We start by defining an instance of a MNL bandit problem.
Let \(\theta_0 = \Pi M_0\) with \( M_0\in\R^{K\times d} \) be defined as follows
\begin{equation*}
M_0 := 
\begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 0 &\dots & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & \dots & 0 \\
    \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
    0 & 0 & \dots & 0
\end{bmatrix} 
\end{equation*}
and \( \rho\in\R^K \) be defined by 
\begin{equation*}
\rho :=
\begin{bmatrix}
    1 \\
    0 \\
    \vdots \\
    0
\end{bmatrix} \,.
\end{equation*}
Even though this define a binary problem, we cannot directly apply the proof of \citet{abeille2021instance} as for \(K\ge 3\) our \(\kappa_*\) will be different than in the binary setting. Indeed the probability distributions of the reward are different, see the \(\ln(K-1)\) term in Eq.\eqref{eq:dist proba in lower bound}.

We define the action set by the sphere \( \X = \mathcal{S}_1(\R^d) \). We show that a slight variation \(M\) of the matrix \(M_0\) results in a regret lower-bounded by \(  \Omega(d\sqrt{T/\kappa_*(\theta)} )\). Let us define the set of perturbed matrices \( \M \) by
\begin{equation*}
    \M := \left\{ M_0 + \epsilon \sum_{i=2}^d v_i e_{1i} \quad , v\in\{-1, 1\}^d \right\} 
\end{equation*}
where \( \epsilon >0\) is to be defined later. For now we only assume that \( \epsilon \le m / \sqrt{d-1} \). Note that we do not modify the first column. We assume that for all \(M\in\M\), we have \( \Reg_T(\Pi M) \le d \sqrt{T/\kappa_*} \). Note if this assumption does not hold, there exists \(M\in\M\) such that \( \Reg_T(\Pi M) \ge \Omega(d \sqrt{T/\kappa_*}) \).

Let \( x_*(\theta) := \argmax_{x\in\X} \rho^\top \mu(\theta x) \). As for \(\theta = \Pi M\) we have \( \mu(\theta x) = \mu(Mx) \), we may abuse the notation and write \( x_*(M) = x_*(\theta) \). For every problem instance \( (\theta = \Pi M \in \Pi\M, \rho, \mathcal{S}_1(\R^d) ) \), we have that \( x_*(\theta) = [M]_1 / \lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 \).

\textbf{Step 1: Lower-bounding by the actions.}

In this step we generalise Proposition~6 from \citet{abeille2021instance}.

Let \(\theta = \Pi M \in \Pi\M\), let us lower-bound \(\Reg_T(\theta)\):
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &:= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho^\top \mu(\theta x_*(\theta)) - \rho^\top \mu(\theta x_t) \\ 
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho^\top \mu(M x_*(\theta)) - \rho^\top \mu(M x_t) &&(\mu(M x) = \mu(\theta x)) \\ 
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho^\top \alpha(M x_*(\theta), M x_t) (M x_*(\theta) - M x_t) &&\text{(Mean-value Theorem)} \\ 
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k=1}^K \rho^\top \alpha(M x_*(\theta), M x_t)_k ([M]_k x_*(\theta) - [M]_k x_t) \\
    &= \dfrac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k=1}^K \rho^\top \alpha(M x_*(\theta), M x_t)_k \rho_k ([M]_1 x_*(\theta) - [M]_1 x_t) &&([M]_k = \tfrac{1}{2} \rho_k [M]_1) \,.
\end{align*}
We focus on \( ([M]_k x_*(\theta) - [M]_k x_t) \), using the definition of \(x_*\) we have that
\begin{equation*}
    ([M]_1 x_*(\theta) - [M]_1 x_t) = \lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 \left( 1 - \tfrac{[M]_1^\top}{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2} x_t \right) = \lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 . \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2
\end{equation*}
where the last equality is due to \( 1 - x^\top y = \lVert x - y \rVert_2^2 \) for all \( x, y \in \mathcal{S}_1(\R^d) \). Thus we obtain
\small
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &= \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2}{2} \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k=1}^K \rho^\top \alpha(M x_*(\theta), M x_t)_k \rho_k \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \\
    &= \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 }{2} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \, \lVert \rho \rVert^2_{\alpha(M x_*(\theta), M x_t)} \\
    &\ge \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 }{2} \dfrac{1}{1+\lVert M(x_*(\theta)-x_t)\rVert_2} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \, \lVert \rho \rVert^2_{ \nabla\mu(M x_*(\theta)) } &&\text{(Self-concordance)} \\
    &\ge \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 }{2} \dfrac{1}{1+2 \lVert M \rVert_2} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \, \lVert \rho \rVert^2_{ \nabla\mu(M x_*(\theta)) } \\
    &= \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 }{2} \dfrac{1}{1+2 \lVert M \rVert_2} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \, \lVert \rho \rVert^2_{ \nabla\mu(\theta x_*(\theta)) } &&(\mu(M x_*(\theta)) = \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))) \\
    &= \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 }{2 \kappa_*(\theta)} \dfrac{1}{1+2 \lVert M \rVert_2} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \,.
\end{align*}
\normalsize
Now note that
\begin{equation*}
    \dfrac{\lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2}{1 + 2\lVert M \rVert_2} = \dfrac{1}{3} \,,
\end{equation*}
which gives
\begin{equation*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) \ge \dfrac{1}{6 \kappa_*(\theta) } \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=1}^d [x_*(\theta) - x_t]_i^2 \,.
\end{equation*}

\textbf{Step 2: Averaging Hammer.}

Following the proof of Lemma~3 of \citet{abeille2021instance} we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inside proof lower bound end step 2}
    \E_\theta[\Reg_T(\theta)] \ge \dfrac{T \epsilon^2}{12 \kappa_*(\theta) } \sum_{i=2}^d \pr_\theta[ A_i(M) ].
\end{equation}

\textbf{Step 3: Average Relative Entropy.}

We now adapt the proof of Lemma~5 of \citet{abeille2021instance}.
Let us denote \( P_{x_t}^{\theta} = \pr_\theta(r|x) \) with \(r\) the reward. Using the Divergence Decomposition Lemma \citep[Exercise~15.8(b)]{lattimore2020bandit} and the fact that the \(\chi^2\)-divergence upper-bounds the KL divergence we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inside proof lower bound 1}
    KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) = \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T KL\left( P_{x_t}^\theta, P_{x_t}^{\flip_i(\theta)} \right) \right] \le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T D_{\chi^2} \left(  P_{x_t}^\theta, P_{x_t}^{\flip_i(\theta)} \right) \right] \,.
\end{equation}
Let us study the distribution \( P_{x_t}^\theta \). We have that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dist proba in lower bound}
    \pr_\theta(\rho_1 | x) = [\mu(Mx)]_1 = \dfrac{\exp([M]_1^\top x)}{\exp([M]_1^\top x) + (K-1)} = \dfrac{1}{1+\exp(-[M]_1^\top x + \ln(K-1))}
\end{equation}
and similarly
\begin{equation*}
    \pr_\theta(\rho_2 | x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + \exp([M]_1^\top  x - \ln(K-1)) } \,.
\end{equation*}
Therefore we have that 
\small
\begin{multline*}
    KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \\
    \le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T  D_{\chi^2} \left( \mathrm{Bernoulli}\left(\mu\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right)\right), \mathrm{Bernoulli}\left(\mu\left( [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right)\right) \right) \right] \,.
\end{multline*}
\normalsize
Using the expression of the \(\chi^2\)-divergence for Bernoulli random variables gives
\begin{equation*}
    KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \dfrac{ \left( \mu\left( [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) - \mu\left( [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \right)^2 }{\mu'\left( [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right)} \right] \,.
\end{equation*}
We apply the Mean-value Theorem and get 
%\begin{multline*}
%    KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \\
%    \le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T  \tfrac{\alpha^2\left( [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1), [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) }{\mu'\left([\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right)} \left(( [M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1 )^\top x_t \right)^2 \right] \,.
%\end{multline*}
\begin{equation*}
    KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) 
    \le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T  \tfrac{\alpha^2\left( [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1), [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) }{\mu'\left([\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right)} \left(( [M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1 )^\top x_t \right)^2 \right] \,.
\end{equation*}
Now applying the self-concordance property gives
\begin{align*}
    &\alpha\left( [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1), [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) \\
    &\qquad \le \mu'\left([\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \exp\left( \left| ([M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1)^\top  x_t \right| \right) \\
    \text{and}& \\
    &\alpha\left( [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1), [\flip_i(M)]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) \\
    &\qquad \le \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \exp\left( \left| ([M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1)^\top  x_t \right| \right) \,.
\end{align*}
Thus we obtain
\footnotesize
\begin{align*}
    KL( &\pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \\
    &\le \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \left(( [M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1 )^\top x_t\right)^2 \exp\left( 2\left| ([M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1)^\top  x_t \right| \right)  \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \left(( [M]_1 - [\flip_i(M)]_1 )^\top x_t\right)^2 \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_t]_i^2 \right] \,.
\end{align*}
\normalsize
We add and subtract \( x_*(\theta) \) and apply Young's inequality:
\begin{align*}
    K&L( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_t - x_*(\theta) + x_*(\theta)]_i^2 \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_t - x_*(\theta)]_i^2 + \sum_{t=1}^T \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_*(\theta)]_i^2 \right] \,.
\end{align*}
Thus by summing over \(d\) we obtain
\footnotesize
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{i=2}^d &KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=2}^d \mu'\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_t - x_*(\theta)]_i^2 + \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=2}^d \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_*(\theta)]_i^2 \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=1}^d \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_t - x_*(\theta)]_i^2 + \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=2}^d \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_*(\theta)]_i^2 \right] \\
    &= \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \lVert x_t - x_*(\theta)\rVert_2^2 + \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=2}^d \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) [x_*(\theta)]_i^2 \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \lVert x_t - x_*(\theta)\rVert_2^2 + \tfrac{(d-1)\epsilon^2}{\lVert [M_0]_1 \rVert_2^2 +(d-1)\epsilon^2} \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \lVert x_t - x_*(\theta)\rVert_2^2 + \tfrac{(d-1)\epsilon^2}{1 +(d-1)\epsilon^2} \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \right] \\
    &\le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \E_\theta \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \lVert x_t - x_*(\theta)\rVert_2^2 + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \right] 
\end{align*}
\normalsize
where for the second to last inequality we use the fact that \( \lVert[M_0]_1 \rVert_2 = 1 \).

\textbf{Step 5: Bounding the First Term of the Average Entropy.}

We upper-bound \( \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \lVert x_t - x_*(\theta)\rVert_2^2 \) by the regret \( \Reg_T(\theta) \). We write the regret using the probabilities of \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\) and get
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho^\top  \mu(\theta x_*(\theta)) - \rho^\top \mu(\theta x_t) \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho_1 \left[ \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta) - \pr_\theta(\rho_1 | x_t) \right] + \rho_2 \left[ \pr_\theta(\rho_2 |x_*(\theta) - \pr_\theta(\rho_2 | x_t) \right]\,.
\end{align*}
Using that \(\rho_1 = 2\) and \(\rho_2=1\) this yields
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &= \sum_{t=1}^T \rho_1 \left[ \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta) - \pr_\theta(\rho_1 | x_t) \right] + \rho_2 \left[ 1- \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta) - 1-\pr_\theta(\rho_1 | x_t) \right] \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta) - \pr_\theta(\rho_1 | x_t) \,.
\end{align*}
We write probabilities as Bernoulli variables and apply the Mean-value Theorem:
\begin{align}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &= \sum_{t=1}^T \mu\left([M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1) \right) -  \mu\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) \nonumber \\
    &= \sum_{t=1}^T \alpha\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1),  [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) . \left( [M]^\top_1 (x_*(\theta)-x_t) \right) \,. \label{eq:inside proof lower bound 2}
\end{align}
Using the self-concordance property we get
\begin{equation*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) \ge \dfrac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1) \right) . \left( [M]^\top_1 (x_*(\theta)-x_t) \right) \,.
\end{equation*}
Recall from Step~1 that \( [M]^\top_1 (x_*(\theta)-x_t)  = \tfrac{1}{2} \lVert [M]_1 \rVert_2 . \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \). We obtain
\begin{align*}
    \Reg_T(\theta) &\ge \dfrac{1}{4} \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1) \right) \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2 \\
    &\ge \dfrac{1}{4} \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1) \right) \lVert x_*(\theta) - x_t \rVert_2^2  \,.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 6: Bounding the Second Term of the Average Entropy.}

In this step, we bound the term \( \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \). We start with a Taylor decomposition with integral remainder:
%\small
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T &\mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \\
    &=\sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1)\right) \\
    &\qquad+ \int_0^1 \mu''\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) + v[M]^\top_1(x_t-x_*(\theta)) -\ln(K-1) \right) dv \left( [M]_1^\top (x_t - x_*(\theta)) \right) \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T  \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1)\right) \\
    &\qquad + \left| \int_0^1 \mu''\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) + v[M]^\top_1 (x_t-x_*(\theta)) -\ln(K-1) \right) dv \right| . \left| [M]_1^\top  (x_t - x_*(\theta)) \right| \,.
\end{align*}
%\normalsize
Using the facts that for the sigmoid \( | \mu''| \le \mu \) and \( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) \ge [M]_1^\top  x_t \) we get
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' &\left([M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1)\right) \\
    &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \mu' \left([M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1)\right) \\
    &\qquad+ \alpha\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) - \ln(K-1), [M]_1^\top  x_t - \ln(K-1) \right) . \left( [M]_1^\top  (x_*(\theta) - x_t) \right) \,.
\end{align*}
Note that the second term is exactly Eq.~\eqref{eq:inside proof lower bound 2}. Using the definition of \(\mu' \) we get 
\begin{align*}
    \mu' &\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) -\ln(K-1) \right) \\
    &= \mu\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) -\ln(K-1) \right) \left( 1-\mu\left( [M]_1^\top  x_*(\theta) -\ln(K-1) \right) \right) \\
    &= \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta)) \left( 1- \pr_\theta(\rho_1 |x_*(\theta)) \right) \\
    &= \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_1 \left( 1 - \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_1 \right) \\
    &\le \sum_{k=1}^K \rho_k^2 \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_k \left( 1 - \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_k \right) &&(\rho_k := \mathbbm{1}[k=1]) \\
    &= \sum_{k=1}^K \rho_k^2 \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_k - \rho_k^2 \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))_k^2 \\
    &= \sum_{k=1}^K \rho^\top  \diag(\mu(\theta x_*(\theta))) \rho - \rho^\top  \mu(\theta x_*(\theta)) \mu(\theta x_*(\theta))^\top  \rho \\
    &= \rho^\top  \nabla \mu(\theta x_*(\theta)) \rho &&(\text{Def of }\nabla\mu) \\
    &\le \dfrac{1}{\kappa_*(\theta)} \,.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Step 7: Putting Everything Together.}
\nopagebreak

Using Step~5 and Step~6 we get
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{i=2}^d KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \left[ 4 \Reg_T(\theta) + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \left( \dfrac{T}{\kappa_*(\theta)} + \Reg_T(\theta) \right) \right] \,.
\end{equation*}
Thus by taking the average
\begin{equation*}
    \dfrac{1}{|\M |} \sum_{M\in\M} \sum_{i=2}^d KL( \pr_\theta, \pr_{\flip_i(\theta)}) \le \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \left[ 4 \Reg_T(\theta) + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \left( \dfrac{T}{\kappa_*(\theta)} + \Reg_T(\theta) \right) \right] \,.
\end{equation*}
Hence using Step~3 we get
\begin{equation*}
    \dfrac{2}{|\M |} \sum_{M\in\M} \sum_{i=2}^d  \pr_\theta[A_i(M)] \ge \tfrac{d}{2} - \sqrt{\tfrac{d-1}{2}} \sqrt{  \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \left[ 4 \Reg_T(\theta) + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \left( \dfrac{T}{\kappa_*(\theta)} + \Reg_T(\theta) \right) \right] } \,.
\end{equation*}
If this is true for the average over \(\M\), then there exists at least one \( M_* \in \M \) such that 
\begin{equation*}
    2 \sum_{i=2}^d  \pr_{\theta_*}[A_i(M_*)] \ge \tfrac{d}{2} - \sqrt{\tfrac{d-1}{2}} \sqrt{ \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \left[ 4 \Reg_T( \theta_*) + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \left( \dfrac{T}{\kappa_*( \theta_*)} + \Reg_T( \theta_*) \right) \right] }
\end{equation*}
where \( \theta_* = \Pi M_* \). Using Step~2 we get 
\small
\begin{align*}
    \E_{ \theta_*} &[\Reg_T(\theta_*)] \\
    &\ge \dfrac{T \epsilon^2}{24 \kappa_*( \theta_*) } \left[ \tfrac{d}{2} - \sqrt{\tfrac{d-1}{2}} \left[ \exp(2\epsilon) \epsilon^2 \left( 4 \Reg_T( \theta_*) + (d-1) \epsilon^2 \left( \dfrac{T}{\kappa_*( \theta_*)} + \Reg_T( \theta_*) \right) \right) \right]^{1/2} \right] \\
    &\ge \dfrac{T \epsilon^2}{24 \kappa_*( \theta_*) } \left[ \tfrac{d}{2} - \tfrac{d}{2} \exp(\epsilon) \left[ 8 \epsilon^2 \sqrt{T/\kappa_*( \theta_*)} + 2\epsilon^4\tfrac{T}{\kappa_*(\theta_*)} + 2\epsilon^4d \sqrt{T/\kappa_*( \theta_*)}  \right]^{1/2} \right] \,.
\end{align*}
\normalsize
We choose \( \epsilon^2 = c \sqrt{\kappa_*( \theta_*)/T} \) with \(c=0.05\) and get
\begin{equation*}
    \E_{ \theta_*} [\Reg_T(\theta_*)] \ge \dfrac{cd\sqrt{T}}{48  \sqrt{\kappa_*( \theta_*)}} \left[ 1 - \exp(\sqrt{c} [\kappa_*( \theta_*)/T]^{1/4} )\left[ 8c + 4 c^2 + 2c^2 d \sqrt{\kappa_*( \theta_*)/T} \right]^{1/2} \right] \,.
\end{equation*}
When \(T\ge d^2 \kappa_*( \theta_*)\) we have that 
\begin{equation*}
    \E_{ \theta_*} [\Reg_T(\theta_*)] \ge \dfrac{cd\sqrt{T}}{48  \sqrt{\kappa_*( \theta_*)}} \left[ 1 - \exp(\sqrt{c})\left[ 8c + 4 c^2 + 2c^2 \right]^{1/2} \right] \ge \dfrac{d\sqrt{T}}{5000  \sqrt{\kappa_*( \theta_*)}} \,.
\end{equation*}

\end{proof}

\section{Proof of Proposition~\ref{thm:computational cost}}\label{appendix:computational cost}

\ThmComputationalCost*

\begin{proof}
Given  \(\theta_{t+1}'\), the matrix \(W_{t+1}\) can be updated from \(W_t\) in \(O(d^2 K^2)\) operations:
\begin{equation*}
    W_{t+1} = W_t + \nabla\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t) \otimes x_t x_t^\top  \,.
\end{equation*}
In order to update the inverse \(W_{t+1}^{-1}\) we compute the Cholesky's decomposition of \( \nabla\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t) \)
\begin{equation*}
    \nabla\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t) = L L^\top 
\end{equation*}
where \(L\in\R^{K\times K} \). By writing \( \smash{\nabla\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t) = \diag(\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t)) - \mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t)\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t)^\top } \) as a rank one update, the Cholesky's decomposition can be computed in \(\smash{O(K^2)}\) operations \citep[Section~6.5.4]{golub2013matrix}.
Thus we can write
\begin{multline*}
    W_{t+1} = W_t + \nabla\mu(\theta_{t+1}' x_t) \otimes x_t x_t^\top  = W_t + L L^\top  \otimes x_t x_t^\top  \\
    = W_t + (L\otimes x_t) ( L^\top  \otimes x_t^\top )= W_t + (L\otimes x_t) ( L \otimes x_t)^\top  = W_t + \sum_{k=1}^K (L_k \otimes x_t) (L_k \otimes x_t)^\top  \,.
\end{multline*}
This decomposition allows us to use the Sherman-Morrison formula \(K\) times to update \( \smash{W_{t+1}^{-1}} \) for a total cost of \( \smash{K^3 d^2} \). We now compute the cost of computing \(\theta_{t+1}' \). Note that \(W_{t+1} \) is positive semi-definite, let \( \smash{W_{t+1} = U_{t+1} U_{t+1}^\top } \) be the Cholesky's decomposition of \( W_{t+1} \). It can be maintained in \( O(K^2 d^2) \) operations thank to the rank one nature of its updates \citep[Section~6.5.4]{golub2013matrix}. Let \( z_t = L_t^\top  \theta_t' \), using the change of variable \(\smash{ z = L_t^\top  \theta} \) we have
\begin{equation*}
    \theta_{t+1}' = L_t^{-\top} \argmin_{L_t^{-\top}z \in \Theta} \left( \bar L_{t+1}(z):= \dfrac{\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \lVert z \rVert^2_2 - \dfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} \langle z, z_t \rangle + \ell_{t+1}(L_t^{-\top}z) \right) \,.
\end{equation*}
We compute the hessian of \( \bar L_{t+1} \) and get
\begin{equation*}
    \nabla^2 \bar L_{t+1}(z) = \dfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} I_{Kd} + \nabla\mu(L_t^{-\top} z x_t) (L_t^{-1}L_t^{-\top} \otimes x_t x_t^\top ) \,.
\end{equation*}
Using that \( W_{t+1}^{-1} \preccurlyeq \lambda^{-1} I_K \preccurlyeq I_K \),  for all \(z\in \R^{K\times d}\)
\begin{equation*}
    \dfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} I_{Kd} \preccurlyeq \nabla^2 \bar L_{t+1}(z) \preccurlyeq \left( \dfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{3} + 1\right) I_{Kd} \,.
\end{equation*}
Therefore \( \bar L_{t+1} \) is strongly-convex and \( \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{2\exp(-\sqrt{6}) + 3} \) well-conditioned. Moreover the set \( \{ z : L_t^{-\top} z \in \Theta \} \) is convex by convexity of \(\Theta\). Let us compute \( \theta_{t+1}' \) using the Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) algorithm for 
\begin{equation*}
    n:= \left( \tfrac{2\exp(-\sqrt{6})}{2\exp(-\sqrt{6}) + 3} + 1 \right) \log(\mathrm{diam}(\Theta)/\epsilon_t)
\end{equation*}
steps. \citep[Lemma~12]{faury2022jointly} ensures that \( \lVert \theta_{t+1} - \theta_{t+1}' \rVert_2 \le \epsilon_t \). At each iteration of Projected Gradient Descent, the cost of computing the gradient is \( \smash{O(K^2 d^2)} \). At each iteration of PGD we also need to project on the set \( \smash{\{ L_t^{-\top} z \in \Theta \}} \). Projecting on this set is done by solving a one-dimensional convex problem \citep[Lemma~13]{faury2022jointly}, which can be done with accuracy \(\epsilon_t\) in \( O(K^2 d^2 \log(1/\epsilon_t)) \).

Finally the total cost of an iteration of Alg.~\ref{algo:learning routine} is \( O( Kd^2 + K^2 + K^3 d^2 + n (K^2 d^2 + K^2 d^2 \log(1/\epsilon_t) )) = O(K^3 d^2 + K^2 d^2 (\log(1/\epsilon_t))^2 ) \).

\end{proof}

\section{Example of large \texorpdfstring{\(\kappa_*\)}{kappa\_*}}\label{appendix:large kappa star}
Let \(K\ge 2\) be even and \(d\ge 1\). Let us consider the following problem, we define \( \theta_* = \Pi M_* \in \Pi\R^{K\times d} \) with \(M_*\) equal to
\begin{equation*}
M_* := 
\begin{bmatrix}
    m & 0 & \dots & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & \dots & 0 \\
    \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
    0 & 0 & \dots & 0
\end{bmatrix} \in \R^d 
\end{equation*}
where \(m>0\), moreover \(M_*\) is such that \( \lVert \theta_* \rVert_2 = S \). We define \(\rho\in\R^K\) such that
\begin{equation*}
\rho :=
\begin{bmatrix}
    1 \\
    0\\
    \vdots \\
    0
\end{bmatrix} \,.
\end{equation*}
We choose \( \X = \mathcal{S}_1(\R^d) \). We have that \( x_* = [M_*]_1/\lVert [M_*]_1 \rVert_2 \). Note that \( \lVert x_* \rVert_2 = 1 = X \). Let us compute \( \kappa_* \):
\begin{align*}
    \kappa_*^{-1} &= \rho^\top \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_*) \rho \\
    &= e_1^\top \nabla\mu(\theta_* x_*)e_1 \\
    &= e_1^\top (\mu(\theta_* x_*)_1 e_1 - \mu(\theta_* x_*)_1 \mu(\theta_* x_*) )  \\
    &= \mu(\theta_* x_*)_1 ( 1- \mu(\theta_* x_*)_1 ) \\
    &= \dfrac{1}{ 1 + (K-1) \exp(-[\theta_*]_1^\top x_*)} \; \dfrac{ (K-1)\exp(-[\theta_*]_1^\top x_*)}{1 + (K-1) \exp(-[\theta_*]_1^\top x_*)} \\
    &= \dfrac{(K-1) \exp(-[\theta_*]_1^\top x_*)}{(1 + (K-1) \exp(-[\theta_*]_1^\top x_*) )^2}  \\
    &= \dfrac{(K-1) \exp(-SX)}{(1 + (K-1) \exp(-SX) )^2} \\
    &\leq (K-1) \exp(-SX) 
\end{align*}
which is exponentially small in $SX$. In this case, by Theorem~\ref{thm:regret bound}, the asymptotic regret is thus of order 
\[
    \Reg_T \leq \tilde O\Big(K^{3/2} d \exp(-SX/2) \sqrt{T} \Big)\,.
\]

\section{Auxiliary Results}\label{appendix:auxiliary results}
\begin{restatable}{lmm}{LmmAux1}[\citet[Section~4.2.3]{boyd2004convex}]\label{lemma:minimiser to gradient positive}
    Let \(f:\R^d\to\R\) be a convex and differentiable function and \(\mathcal{C} \subseteq \R^d\) a convex set. Further, denote:
    \begin{equation*}
        x_0 := \argmin_{x_0\in\mathcal{C}} f(x) \,.
    \end{equation*}
    Then for any \(y\in\mathcal{C}\):
    \begin{equation*}
        \nabla f(x_0)^\top  (y-x_0) \ge 0 \,.
    \end{equation*}
\end{restatable}

\begin{restatable}{lmm}{LmmAux2}[Modified Freedman's Inequality,  \citet[Lemma~3]{lee2024improved}]\label{lemma:modified Freedman inequality}
    Let \( X_1, \dots, X_t \) be a martingale difference sequence satisfying \(\max_s |X_s| \le D \) a.s., and let \(\F_s \) be the \(\sigma\)-field generated by \( (X_1, \dots, X_s) \). Then for any \(\delta\in(0, 1] \) and any \( \eta \in [0, 1/D]  \) the following holds with probability \(1-\delta\)
    \begin{equation*}
        \sum_{s=1}^t X_s \le (e-2) \eta \sum_{s=1}^t \E[X_s^2 | \F_{s-1}] + \dfrac{1}{\eta} \log \delta^{-1} \qquad \forall t \ge 1 \,.
    \end{equation*}
\end{restatable}

\begin{restatable}{lmm}{LmmDetTraceInequality}[Determinant-Trace Inequality,  \citet[Lemma~10]{abbasi2011improved}]\label{lemma:det_trace inequality}
    Let \( \{x_s\}_{s=1}^{\infty} \) be a sequence in \(\R^d\) such that \(\lVert x_s \rVert_2 \le X \) for all \(s\ge1\), and let \(\lambda\ge 0\). For \( t\ge1 \) define \( V_t := \sum_{s=1}^t x_s x_s^\top  + \lambda I_d \). The following inequality holds:
    \begin{equation*}
        \det(V_t) \le (\lambda + t X^2 / d )^d \,.
    \end{equation*}
\end{restatable}

title: History of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots: past, present, and future development
summary:
This research provides an in-depth comprehensive review of the progress of
chatbot technology over time, from the initial basic systems relying on rules
to today's advanced conversational bots powered by artificial intelligence.
Spanning many decades, the paper explores the major milestones, innovations,
and paradigm shifts that have driven the evolution of chatbots. Looking back at
the very basic statistical model in 1906 via the early chatbots, such as ELIZA
and ALICE in the 1960s and 1970s, the study traces key innovations leading to
today's advanced conversational agents, such as ChatGPT and Google Bard. The
study synthesizes insights from academic literature and industry sources to
highlight crucial milestones, including the introduction of Turing tests,
influential projects such as CALO, and recent transformer-based models. Tracing
the path forward, the paper highlights how natural language processing and
machine learning have been integrated into modern chatbots for more
sophisticated capabilities. This chronological survey of the chatbot landscape
provides a holistic reference to understand the technological and historical
factors propelling conversational AI. By synthesizing learnings from this
historical analysis, the research offers important context about the
developmental trajectory of chatbots and their immense future potential across
various field of application which could be the potential take ways for the
respective research community and stakeholders.

title: Uniform Validity of the Subset Anderson-Rubin Test under Heteroskedasticity and Nonlinearity
summary:
We consider the Anderson-Rubin (AR) statistic for a general set of nonlinear
moment restrictions. The statistic is based on the criterion function of the
continuous updating estimator (CUE) for a subset of parameters not constrained
under the Null. We treat the data distribution nonparametrically with
parametric moment restrictions imposed under the Null. We show that subset
tests and confidence intervals based on the AR statistic are uniformly valid
over a wide range of distributions that include moment restrictions with
general forms of heteroskedasticity. We show that the AR based tests have
correct asymptotic size when parameters are unidentified, partially identified,
weakly or strongly identified. We obtain these results by constructing an upper
bound that is using a novel perturbation and regularization approach applied to
the first order conditions of the CUE. Our theory applies to both
cross-sections and time series data and does not assume stationarity in time
series settings or homogeneity in cross-sectional settings.

\title{Uniform Validity of the Subset Anderson-Rubin Test under Heteroskedasticity
and Nonlinearity\hspace{2pt}\thanks{We thank participants of the Econometrics Workshop at Notre Dame 2024
and seminar participants at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for

\begin{abstract}
{\normalsize We consider the Anderson-Rubin (AR) statistic for a general
set of nonlinear moment restrictions. The statistic is based on the
criterion function of the continuous updating estimator (CUE) for
a subset of parameters not constrained under the Null. We treat the
data distribution nonparametrically with parametric moment restrictions
imposed under the Null. We show that subset tests and confidence intervals
based on the AR statistic are uniformly valid over a wide range of
distributions that include moment restrictions with general forms
of heteroskedasticity. We show that the AR based tests have correct
asymptotic size when parameters are unidentified, partially identified,
weakly or strongly identified. We obtain these results by constructing
an upper bound that is using a novel perturbation and regularization
approach applied to the first order conditions of the CUE. Our theory
applies to both cross-sections and time series data and does not assume
stationarity in time series settings or homogeneity in cross-sectional
settings.}{\normalsize\par}
\end{abstract}
\bigskip{}
\noindent{} \emph{JEL classification codes:} C11, C12, C22, C32, C44.

\bigskip{}
\noindent\emph{Keywords:} uniformly valid inference, lack of identification,
local projection, impulse response. \bigskip{}
\noindent{}

\section{Introduction}
